note.kid: The address label: who it’s from and who it’s for. Every router on the way reads it.
note.nerd: Best-effort delivery between any two addresses on the internet: routers forward it on the destination address, hop by hop.

version.name: Version
version.about: Which IP this is: 4 (IPv6 packets say 6).

dscp.name: DSCP
dscp.about: Traffic class, for networks that give some traffic priority.

ecn.name: ECN
ecn.about: Lets a busy router mark the packet instead of dropping it.

length.name: Total length
length.about: Bytes in this packet, header and all.

id.name: Identification
id.about: Ties fragments together if the packet is ever split.

flags.name: Flags
flags.about: DF: don’t fragment. Too big for a link? Drop it and say so (path MTU discovery).

frag.name: Fragment offset
frag.about: Where this fragment belongs; 0 when not split.

ttl.about: Every router takes one off and drops the packet at 0, so a routing loop can’t keep it forever.

proto.name: Protocol
proto.about: What is inside: 6 = TCP. Routers hash it with the addresses and ports (the 5-tuple) to pick one of several equal paths (ECMP).

checksum.name: Header checksum
checksum.about: Checked by every router, and rewritten because the TTL changed.

src.about: Who sent it, as seen here: a NAT rewrites it to its own outside address.

dst.about: Where it’s going: routers look it up in their forwarding table (longest prefix match).
